skill.name: sandbox-configurator
skill.description: Configure Claude Code sandbox settings for file access, network access, Docker use, and trusted development workflows.
skill.summary: Build Claude Code sandbox policies with clear security trade-offs.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The scanned files are documentation and a process diagram, not executable code. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, inline command names, and example secret variable names, but the skill does include guidance for disabling or weakening sandbox protections.

remediation.issue: No-sandbox and development modes weaken execution isolation.
remediation.suggestion: Make maximum security the default, remove no-sandbox as a preset, and require explicit user confirmation before recommending local binding, Unix sockets, or excluded commands.

remediation.issue: Docker and Git exclusions can bypass sandbox controls.
remediation.suggestion: Explain the exact trust boundary change for each excluded command and recommend the smallest set needed for the current workflow.

remediation.issue: Example environment variables use secret-like names.
remediation.suggestion: Replace token and API key examples with non-secret placeholders, and document secret storage outside shared settings files.

static_findings.snippet: - **Blocked Docker commands**: Add docker to `excludedCommands` and enable `allowUnixSockets`
- **Package installation blocked**: Add package registry to `trustedDomains`

content.value_statement: Sandbox settings are hard to balance when projects need networks, Docker, or local servers. This skill guides Claude Code policy choices with clear trade-offs.
actual_capabilities: Maps project needs to maximum, balanced, development, or custom sandbox profiles.
Defines trusted domains for package registries, GitHub, and internal services.
Explains local binding, Unix socket, Docker, and Git trade-offs.
Produces a sandbox configuration plan for Claude Code settings.
Provides validation checks for package installs, Git, Docker, and dev servers.
Documents security decisions so teams can review the chosen policy.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not enforce sandbox settings by itself.
It cannot prove that a runtime sandbox is correctly isolated after setup.
Development and no-sandbox options can create high risk if approved carelessly.
Secret handling must be reviewed before adding environment variables.

use_cases.title: Harden open source contribution workspaces
use_cases.description: Use a maximum security profile with public registries only and minimal command exclusions.

use_cases.title: Balance enterprise development access
use_cases.description: Choose trusted internal domains, required build variables, and documented exceptions for approved workflows.

use_cases.title: Review local full-stack sandbox needs
use_cases.description: Evaluate local servers, Docker, Git, and registry access before granting broader permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a secure default
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure a maximum security Claude Code sandbox for this project. Allow only package registries and GitHub if they are necessary.

prompt_templates.title: Support a local web app
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a balanced sandbox plan for a full-stack app that needs package installs, Git, Docker, and a local development server.

prompt_templates.title: Fit enterprise network rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a sandbox policy for an enterprise repository with internal registries, approved domains, and required build variables. Explain every exception.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an existing policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current Claude Code sandbox policy. Identify unnecessary access, risky exclusions, secret-handling issues, and safer alternatives.

output_examples.input: I need a safe setup for contributing to an unfamiliar open source repository.
output: Trusted access limited to public package registries and GitHub.
Local binding, Docker sockets, and broad command exclusions remain disabled.
Validation focuses on install, test, and read-only repository workflows.

output_examples.input: My full-stack project needs Docker and a local development server.
output: Balanced profile selected with explicit exceptions.
Local binding is allowed for the development server only.
Docker access is treated as a higher-risk exception that needs team approval.
The final plan explains each security trade-off.

output_examples.input: Audit my existing sandbox settings for unnecessary access.
output: The review highlights broad trusted domains, unused command exclusions, and secret-like variables.
It recommends narrower domains, fewer exclusions, and separate secret storage.
It lists validation checks to confirm the safer policy still supports the workflow.

best_practices: Start with maximum security and add only the access required for the current workflow.
Document why each trusted domain, local binding rule, socket, and command exclusion is needed.
Keep secrets out of shared sandbox configuration and use approved secret storage.
anti_patterns: Using no-sandbox mode for unfamiliar code or untrusted repositories.
Adding broad wildcard domains before confirming the exact services required.
Excluding Git, Docker, or shell workflows without recording the security impact.

faq.question: Does this skill change my sandbox settings automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a configuration plan and validation checklist for Claude Code sandbox settings.

faq.question: Which security level should I start with?
faq.answer: Start with maximum security. Move to a broader profile only when a required workflow is blocked.

faq.question: Can it support Docker workflows?
faq.answer: Yes, it can describe Docker access, Unix socket needs, and the security impact of enabling them.

faq.question: Does it handle network allowlists?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps define trusted domains for registries, GitHub, and approved internal services.

faq.question: Can it review an existing sandbox policy?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare current settings against the requested workflow and recommend tighter boundaries.

faq.question: Is no-sandbox mode safe?
faq.answer: No. No-sandbox mode gives direct system access and should be avoided for untrusted code.
